chunks: One of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'We eat the ushnana.' He said: 'Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when he performed ablution with it, closed his lips. And in it is an abhorrent quality: it causes tuberculosis, removes the water of the back, and weakens the knees.' I said, 'And what about the clay?' He said: 'Every clay is prohibited, like the dead body, blood, and flesh of the pig, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for indeed in it is a healing from every illness, but do not use it excessively, and in it is security from every fear.'

key_terms.الْأُشْنَان: Ushnana, a salt-water plant used for ablution

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating ushnana and clay in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general clay (turbah) and the specific blessed earth of Imam al-Husayn (AS), elevating it from mere ritual purity to a spiritual remedy. While the text notes physical detestable traits of 'ushnana, the core theological emphasis lies in the unique status of Karbala’s soil as a source of healing (shifa) and protection (aman), reflecting the Shia practice of prostrating on the Imam's turbah. This practice underscores the belief in the intercessory and metaphysical power of the Ahl al-Bayt's physical remains.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from Sa’ad who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I eat the saltwort’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> performed ablution (with saltwort), closed his<sup>asws</sup> lips, and in it is an abhorrent quality, it inherits the tuberculosis, and does away with the water of the back, and weakens the knees’. 
So I said, ‘So (what about) the clay?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every clay is Prohibited (to eat), like the dead, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, except for the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, for therein is a healing from every illness, but do not frequent from it, and in it is a security from every fear’.
en.sarwar: 2. Certain persons of our people have narrated from Ja‘far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadramiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I eat saltwort.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when washing his hands and mouth (with saltwort) would keep his lips closed. There is a quality in it, which is disliked. It can cause tuberculoses, it takes away the water of the back and weakens the knees.’ I then asked about clay. He (the Imam) said, ‘Eating clay is unlawful like dead bodies, blood and pork except the clay and soil of the grave of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in which there is cure for all illnesses, however, do not be excessive, and there is immunity in it against all kinds of fear.’”
